transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Rhea (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maya (Saffron CTO), Carlos (VP Eng), Asha (Head of Data), Priya (Security)

Summary: quick intro, goals for pilot, high level architecture options, security requirements, timeline and owners

[00:00] Liam Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Liam from Redwood, AE on the account, with Rhea our solutions engineer and Jordan our CSM. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Dr. Maya Singh: Good, thanks. Excited to get started. We wanted to use this to align on scope and next steps.
[00:20] Carlos Ortega: Yeah we have a couple of goals - get a safe pilot in prod-ish environment, validate latency for our patient messaging flows, and make sure data residency and compliance are squared away.
[00:35] Liam Patel: Totally. today we'll run through deployment modes, security and compliance asks, pilot success criteria, and then set owners and dates. Rhea, want to cover hosting options?
[00:44] Rhea Nguyen: Sure. So Redwood offers hosted API, Redwood Dedicated which is reserved GPU capacity, and Redwood Private which can be VPC or on-prem. For pilot people usually pick Dedicated or Private if they need isolation.
[00:59] Priya Menon: For Saffron, we need network isolation and audit logs, also KMS integration for keys. SOC2 attestation is required from vendors.
[01:10] Jordan Kim: We can share our compliance pack includes SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and our data retention policy. I'll drop links in the follow up.
[01:20] Asha Rao: Great. on the technical side, we care about latency for chat experiences, and token costs; can you share typical p50/p95 numbers for Dedicated?
[01:32] Rhea Nguyen: Yes. rough numbers depend on model and sequence length, but for the models we recommend, p50 latencies are usually sub-200ms for short prompts on Dedicated with batching tuned. p95 can go up during bursts; we have smart routing and fallback to smaller variants to keep SLOs. note: these are approximates, we'll run an exact bench with your payloads.
[01:53] Carlos Ortega: ok, we will need an apples-to-apples bench. we use ~300 tokens average and some long context for certain flows.
[02:02] Rhea Nguyen: Perfect, we'll need sample prompts and traffic profile. Also want to highlight prefix/K-V cache - we sometimes call it K-V cache in the runtime and it helps reduce token throughput for repeated prefixes.
[02:15] Dr. Maya Singh: Is KV cache available on Dedicated?
[02:18] Rhea Nguyen: Yes, KV cache and batching optimizations are available on Dedicated and Private. On hosted we have caching but there are tenancy limits.
[02:27] Priya Menon: For Private, we need to confirm network diagrams and whether Redwood control plane touches customer VPC.
[02:33] Liam Patel: For Private we do offer a customer-managed control plane option; in VPC mode the data plane sits in your VPC and control plane minimal calls are over a managed channel. We'll share an architecture doc.
[02:45] Priya Menon: ok please send diagrams. Also need to confirm SAML SSO integration for our engineers and audit log retention (7 years for us ideally).
[02:55] Jordan Kim: Our default audit logs retention is 1 year but we have options for extended retention as an add-on. I'll include details and pricing in the follow up.
[03:05] Carlos Ortega: On billing, how does reserved Dedicated pricing work? monthly commit?
[03:10] Liam Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits. We can provide a quote based on expected throughput. For pilot we often do a short-term reserved pool or burstable demo capacity.
[03:22] Asha Rao: Do you support BYO KMS/HSM?
[03:25] Rhea Nguyen: Yes, KMS integrations are supported for dedicated/private, and for private on-prem we have HSM options. We'll need to capture your KMS provider.
[03:33] Dr. Maya Singh: Security team will want to run a questionnaire and a quick VAPT. Is that ok?
[03:38] Priya Menon: yep that's standard.
[03:41] Liam Patel: Absolutely, we welcome the questionnaire. Jordan will send the security docs and the SOC2.
[03:46] Jordan Kim: I'll send the full pack after the call.
[03:50] Rhea Nguyen: For the pilot scope - propose we start with these three routes: 1) a hosted evaluation for quick integration and feature validation, 2) Dedicated reserved pool for performance validation on your traffic, and 3) Private/VPC for security checks if needed. We can run the hosted eval while we provision Dedicated.
[04:10] Carlos Ortega: That makes sense. Our timeline: want to start dev integration in July and run a 4-week pilot by August.
[04:18] Liam Patel: Good, that matches Redwood's typical onboard. For success criteria what are the measurable items?
[04:24] Dr. Maya Singh: latency under 300ms p95 for messaging flows, error rate <0.5% during pilot, and security artifacts in place.
[04:32] Asha Rao: Also need cost per 1k tokens to be roughly in the expected band, we'll validate.
[04:38] Rhea Nguyen: We'll run cost modeling with your token counts. For tooling we have Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization to reduce unit cost.
[04:46] Carlos Ortega: Are there known model suggestions for lower cost vs quality?
[04:50] Rhea Nguyen: Yes, we curate model catalog entries and suggest quantized variants; we can recommend based on your loss tolerance. For sensitive data you can also redact at ingest or use private models.
[04:59] Priya Menon: Data residency - we need EU only for certain workloads. is that supported?
[05:04] Liam Patel: We support region pinning for hosted and Dedicated in our EU region; Private can be completely on-prem. We'll note this in the doc.
[05:12] Dr. Maya Singh: ok good. next -- integration specifics. What are the SDKs and how fast to get devs started?
[05:18] Rhea Nguyen: We have REST and SDKs in Python/Node/Go. For quickstarts we have templates and a sample repo. Typical devs can get a call returning in hours if they stub API keys.
[05:28] Carlos Ortega: Any rate limits on hosted during pilot?
[05:30] Jordan Kim: We'll give pilot customers relaxed rate limits, and Dedicated has dedicated throughput.
[05:36] Asha Rao: For benching, we'll provide sample prompts and a spike traffic pattern. Who will run the bench from Redwood side?
[05:42] Rhea Nguyen: I will run the bench with support from infra. We'll coordinate on exact commit and test harness.
[05:48] Liam Patel: ok, let's tie owners. Action item recap coming up.
[05:52] Dr. Maya Singh: One more - do you store user data? retention after inference?
[05:56] Jordan Kim: By default we don't retain customer prompts for model training unless opted in; we'll include that in the data handling doc.
[06:04] Priya Menon: good to have that explicit in the security pack.
[06:08] Carlos Ortega: timeline again - we need SSO test creds by next week ideally.
[06:13] Priya Menon: I'll provision a SAML test app and share next update by 2026-07-05.
[06:19] Liam Patel: Great. For the deep-dive on private deployment Rhea, you said 7/7 is possible?
[06:24] Rhea Nguyen: I can do 7/7 or 7/8, I'll send a calendar invite. We'll bring infra and runtime folks for kernel/quantization discussions if you want deep perf tuning.
[06:36] Asha Rao: yes please include perf people. Also will you share the benchmark template?
[06:40] Rhea Nguyen: Yes I'll share a spreadsheet with fields for prompt sets, token counts, concurrency, and expected SLOs.
[06:46] Liam Patel: Anything else from Saffron team?
[06:49] Carlos Ortega: No, that's it.
[06:51] Dr. Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
[06:53] Liam Patel: Okay recap of next steps: I'll send onboarding deck, pricing, SOC2 pack; Rhea will schedule deep-dive and share benchmark template; Priya will provide SSO test credentials; Jordan will send audit/log retention options and links. We'll set a follow-up in two weeks to review progress.
[07:12] Jordan Kim: I'll put together the links and action item tracker.
[07:18] Liam Patel: thanks all. meeting closing.

Notes about transcription: some words may be mis-heard (e.g., K-V cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache), product names sometimes echoed as Redwood Dedicated or RedWood Dedicatd in auto transcript. Links to docs to be included in follow-up email (onboarding deck, SOC2, network diagrams, benchmark template).

End of transcript.
